title: Butter Chicken
subtitle: Tender chicken in a velvety spiced tomato and cream sauce
excerpt: Butter chicken is one of the best-known curries outside India. The chicken is first marinated in yoghurt and spices, then cooked and folded into a rich tomato sauce finished with cream and butter. The result is mild enough for most palates but complex enough to keep you interested.
sourceNotes: Butter chicken was created at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, likely in the 1950s, as a way to use leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a tomato and butter sauce. It became one of the most widely eaten Indian dishes globally.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the sauce (without the cream) for up to 3 months. Add cream when reheating.

content.text: Marinating overnight gives noticeably better flavour and colour on the chicken. If you are short on time, even 30 minutes makes a difference over skipping the marinade entirely.

content.text: Mix the greek yoghurt, lemon juice, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp cumin-ground, half the garlic, half the ginger, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Add the chicken, coat well, and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Heat the sunflower oil in the frying pan over high heat. Cook the marinated chicken in batches until charred in places and cooked through, around 5 minutes per batch. Set aside.

Melt the butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until golden. Add the remaining garlic, ginger, coriander, turmeric, paprika, cardamom, cinnamon, and remaining cumin and garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and 100 ml of water. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Use a blender or stick blender to blitz until smooth, then return to the pan.
Add the cooked chicken to the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the double cream and simmer for a further 5 minutes. Taste, adjust seasoning, and serve with rice or naan.

items.cause: The tinned tomatoes were not cooked down long enough to mellow
items.fix: Continue simmering uncovered, or add a pinch of sugar to balance the acidity.

items.cause: Chicken breast can dry out quickly over high heat
items.fix: Next time, use chicken thighs, which are more forgiving. If serving now, the sauce will help re-moisten the meat.
